summary: Decrypto is a team-based clue-giving and code-cracking party game where each team tries to communicate secret words to teammates using number-coded clues, while the opposing team listens in trying to intercept the code. It plays fast, gets loud and tense, and rewards clever, ambiguous-to-outsiders-but-clear-to-teammates clue-giving.
praised: Extremely clever core hook of dual-purpose clues
Scales well and generates big table talk and laughter
Great for mixed groups of gamers and non-gamers
criticised: Requires roughly even team sizes and engaged players
Can feel unbalanced if one team is much better at clue-giving
Pen-and-paper tracking is a bit fiddly
Less fun with only 3-4 players total

interaction.kind: intercepting and deciphering the opposing team's coded clues while protecting your own
interaction.detail: Every clue you give is heard by the opposing team, who are actively trying to decode it, and you spend your turn simultaneously trying to break their code — so each team's actions are read directly against the other's. There's no private board at all; the entire game state (the clue history and interceptions) is shared and adversarial.
interaction.said: unknown — but the design is explicitly built around teams trying to crack each other's codes

sources: miscommunication tokens against your own team
interception tokens earned by the opposing team decoding your clues
scoring.how_you_win: Your team loses immediately if you rack up 2 miscommunication tokens or the opposing team correctly intercepts 2 of your codes; if 8 rounds pass without either happening, the team with fewer total bad tokens wins.
